angle: AI won’t kill apps; it raises the bar for workflow design, governance, and change.
linkedinPost:
“Everyone will build their own app with AI” is a comforting story—and a trap.

Benedict Evans argues that imagining AI turns everyone into tool-builders misunderstands how software gets made and how companies actually work. I agree. In the enterprise, apps aren’t dead; ownership, permissions, compliance, and support don’t disappear because you can prompt.

My take: AI is a new UI and automation layer, not a substitute for product management. The winners design opinionated workflows with embedded guardrails, connect them to systems of record, and define who owns outcomes. The losers ship a blank chat box and call it “transformation.”

A practical checklist I use: start with one painful workflow, write the success metric in business terms, constrain the model’s playground, capture feedback in the tool, and train the team like it’s a new process (because it is).

Where have you seen “ask the model” flop—and what did you replace it with that people actually use? #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI #DigitalTransformation
